question: How do you implement API versioning in Django REST Framework?
title: API Versioning in DRF
direct_answer: DRF supports URL path versioning (/api/v1/, /api/v2/), header versioning (Accept: application/json; version=2), and query parameter versioning (?version=2). URL versioning is the most explicit and SEO-friendly. Set DEFAULT_VERSIONING_CLASS in REST_FRAMEWORK settings. Access the version in views via request.version. Use versioned serializers (if request.version == 'v2': use V2Serializer) or separate viewsets per version.

seo.metaDescription: Django REST Framework API versioning: URL path versioning, request.version access, versioned serializers, and migration strategy.

speakable_v2.hook: URL versioning is explicit — /api/v2/users/ is clearly different from /api/v1/users/ and clients can't accidentally hit the wrong version.

beats.content: Add <version> to your URL pattern. DRF populates request.version from the URL. Branch on it in get_serializer_class() for different response shapes.
Maintain v1 while clients migrate to v2. Set a sunset date. Return Sunset header on v1 responses to signal deprecation.

speakable_v2.cap: Header versioning (Accept: application/json; version=2) is harder to test in browsers and Swagger. URL versioning is more debuggable.
speakable_v2.followup_handoff: Follow up with Sunset header for deprecation signaling, or how to structure separate serializer modules per API version.
